title: Hybrid NLB→ALB ingress Terraform module: TLS passthrough, connection draining, and health-probe orchestration
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
Design and implement a reusable Terraform module for internal VPC ingress that supports a hybrid NLB -> ALB pattern with two TLS modes: (1) TLS passthrough for workloads that require client certificate preservation (mTLS) and raw TCP forwarding, and (2) TLS termination at the ALB for HTTP(s) path/host routing. The module should automate Target Groups, listeners, security group wiring, connection draining (deregistration_delay), and a healthcheck orchestration layer that supports HTTP, HTTPS, and TCP health probes and a readiness gate for gradual rollouts.

Motivation:
- Some on-prem/private workloads require preserving client certs for mTLS and cannot have ALB terminate TLS. AWS NLB supports passthrough; we need a consistent terraform pattern to combine NLB's L4 features with ALB's L7 routing when desired.
- Current infra has ad-hoc scripts and manual steps that cause rollback friction during upgrades and inconsistent health-check config across services.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Hybrid topology: place an internal NLB in front of one or more ALBs. NLB will handle SNI/TCP passthrough and client IP preservation; ALB will be optional (only for services needing L7 routing). Trade-off: added complexity and slightly higher maintenance vs. single ALB. We favored predictable client-certificate behavior and cross-AZ balancing.
- TLS modes: module exposes a per-service flag ingress_tls_mode: ["passthrough","terminate"]. "passthrough" creates an NLB TLS listener with forwarding to a target group of instances/pods (preserves cert). "terminate" creates NLB TCP listener that forwards to ALB where TLS is terminated; ALB has HTTPS listener with ACM cert.
- Healthchecks: for "passthrough" we default to TCP health checks (fast, low overhead). For "terminate" we default to HTTP/HTTPS with path /_infra/healthz including an auth token header for better signal. We also add active canary probes: an ALB target group tag can enable canary-probe-runner which calls the health URL with production-like headers. Trade-off: HTTP probes are more expressive but require app changes to surface a stable health path.
- Connection draining: default deregistration_delay = 300s (5m) configurable per-target-group. Required for long-lived streaming connections.
- Security: module supports mutual TLS between ALB→backend via client cert injection or target-side TLS; also integrates with KMS for storing private keys if the flow terminates at the ALB and we manage certs. We require the security_review_required flag for any tenant enabling termination.

Acceptance criteria (what counts as done):
- Terraform module published in modules/ingress/nlb-alb-hybrid with examples: passthrough-only, terminate-only, and hybrid path-based routing examples.
- Module exposes variables: ingress_tls_mode, certificate_arn, deregistration_delay, healthcheck_type, healthcheck_path, healthy_threshold, unhealthy_threshold, canary_probe_enabled, internal_subnet_ids, cross_zone_load_balancing, ip_target_type.
- Integration test infra (small ephemeral stack) in ci/integration/ that exercises service rollout with canary probe and verifies no traffic loss during connection draining.
- Docs: README with topology diagrams, config examples, recommended parameter sets for gRPC, websocket, and HTTP APIs; migration guide for existing stacks.
- Security review completed and documented in Confluence: /confluence/redwood/private-ingress-security-review/ENG-55234.

Implementation notes / progress updates:
- 2026-02-12: Spike completed. Validated NLB passthrough + ALB termination pattern in staging account; saw correct client IP preservation and TLS passthrough when NLB listener type = TLS with target group type = instance/ip.
- 2026-02-18: First Terraform module skeleton committed: github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules/pull/1025. Module structure follows our standard patterns (variables.tf, outputs.tf, examples/, test/).
- 2026-02-24: Decided to prefer separate target groups per TLS mode to simplify lifecycle and enable per-target-group deregistration_delay. Documented this in design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/NLB-ALB+Hybrid+Ingress+Design.
- 2026-03-02: Added health-probe orchestration layer concept. Implementation approach: use a small AWS Lambda (probe-runner) invoked by CloudWatch Events to perform canary checks when canary_probe_enabled=true. Probe results are written to SSM Parameter Store and used as an external readiness gate (we add a Lambda-backed step in our rollout automation to consult SSM before routing 100%). Implementation PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules/pull/1058 (WIP).
- 2026-03-08: Security review kickoff with Security team; initial notes: require telemetry for TLS termination (audit logs of cert usage), enforce TLS 1.2+ listener policies, and explicit ACLs.

Open technical questions / blockers:
- Cross-account ACM handling: if customers bring ACM certs in another account/private cert store, module needs an option to accept cert ARN or import cert via Secrets Manager. Engineering to decide on supported integration pattern.
- How to configure ALB redirect from HTTP→HTTPS consistently for internal-only ALBs? We need to avoid accidental public redirects; add explicit boolean enable_http_redirect.
- Probe-runner IAM boundary: least privilege policy is drafted but needs Security sign-off.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (dev accounts): land module with passthrough-only example; verify healthchecks and connection draining on ephemeral services.
- Stage 2 (staging): enable hybrid mode with ALB termination for a single non-critical service; run integration test workflow and monitor Console cost & latency dashboards for anomalies.
- Stage 3 (canary): enable for a small subset of private workloads behind feature-flagged infra; use probe-runner readiness gate to automate 30%→100% rollout over 1h windows, with auto-fallback to previous TG on errors.
- Rollback path: revert terraform changes and re-register previous target-groups; for rapid rollback, remove NLB new listeners and rely on ALB-only path if available (pre-provisioned). Document steps in runbook.

QA checklist:
- Verify target registration/deregistration respects deregistration_delay during pod/instance termination.
- Confirm client IP addresses appear in X-Forwarded-For (for ALB termination) or preserved at backend (for passthrough).
- Confirm TLS modes behave: client cert visible to backend in passthrough; ALB termination validates SNI and serves correct cert.
- Validate IAM least-privilege for probe-runner and Terraform execution role.
- Run chaos test: terminate backend instances and ensure no 502 spike beyond baseline during graceful draining.

Next steps (owner: Marco Reyes):
- Complete PR 1058 (probe-runner) and attach IAM policy template. Target merge by 2026-03-15.
- Address security feedback items: TLS minimum versions & logging.
- Add migration script for existing stacks that rely on ALB-only patterns to opt into passthrough without downtime.
